content: The American Dental Association (ADA) is a professional organization in the United States that advocates for oral health care and the field of dentistry. It was founded in 1859 and currently has over 152,000 members. Headquartered in Chicago, the ADA is the largest and oldest national dental association in the world. Its mission includes promoting good oral health to the public and representing the dental profession. The ADA publishes a monthly journal called the Journal of the American Dental Association (JADA), which features articles related to dentistry. The ADA was established on August 1859 in Niagara Falls, New York, by 26 dentists representing various dental societies across the United States. Today, the organization includes 55 constituent (state-territorial) and 545 component (local) dental societies. It remains the largest and oldest national dental association globally. The ADA Foundation operates the Paffenbarger Research Center (PRC), located on the campus of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in Gaithersburg, Maryland. This center conducts both basic and applied research in areas such as clinical studies, dental chemistry, polymer chemistry, and cariology. The ADA has also established rigorous guidelines for testing and advertising dental products. The first ADA Seal of Acceptance was awarded in 1931, and today, approximately 350 manufacturers participate in the voluntary program, with over 1,300 products receiving the Seal. The ADA's administrative body, the Board of Trustees, consists of the President, President-elect, two Vice Presidents, and 17 trustees representing the 17 trustee districts in the United States. The Treasurer and Executive Director serve as ex officio members. The legislative body, the House of Delegates, is composed of 460 delegates representing 53 constituent societies, five federal dental services, and the American Student Dental Association. The House meets annually during the ADA's annual session. The ADA also has 11 councils that serve as policy-recommending agencies, each focusing on specific areas of interest and making recommendations to the Board of Trustees and the House of Delegates. The ADA's official publication is the Journal of the American Dental Association (JADA). Other publications include ADA News and the ADA Guide to Dental Therapeutics. The ADA is recognized by the U.S. Department of Education as the national accrediting body for dental, advanced dental, and allied dental education programs. It formally recognizes nine specialty areas in dental practice: dental public health, endodontics, oral and maxillofacial pathology, oral and maxillofacial surgery, orthodontics and dentofacial orthopedics, pediatric dentistry, periodontics, prosthodontics, and oral and maxillofacial radiology. The ADA library houses an extensive collection of dental literature, including approximately 33,000 books and 17,500 bound journal volumes. It also subscribes to more than 600 journal titles. The ADA Foundation serves as the charitable arm of the organization, providing grants for dental research, education, scholarships, access to care, and charitable assistance programs. These programs include relief grants for dentists and their dependents who are unable to support themselves due to injury, medical conditions, or advanced age, as well as grants for victims of disasters. Significant Events in ADA History: 1840: The first dental college, the Baltimore College of Dental Surgery, is established. The American Society of Dental Surgeons is also founded. 1845: The American Society of Dental Surgeons requires members to pledge not to use amalgam fillings. 1856: The American Society of Dental Surgeons disbands due to its stance against dental amalgam, leading to a loss of membership. 1859: Twenty-six dentists meet in Niagara Falls, New York, to form a professional society. 1860: The first ADA constitution and bylaws are adopted. 1897: The ADA merges with the Southern Dental Association to form the National Dental Association (NDA). 1908: The NDA publishes the first patient dental education pamphlet. 1913: The NDA adopts a new constitution and bylaws, establishing the House of Delegates and Board of Trustees. The Journal of the National Dental Association is first published under the title Bulletin of the National Dental Association. 1922: The NDA is renamed the American Dental Association (ADA). 1928: The ADA affiliates with the National Bureau of Standards (NBS), and the National Board of Dental Examiners is established. 1930: The Council of Dental Therapeutics is established to oversee the evaluation of dental products, leading to the creation of the ADA's Seal Program. 1931: The first ADA Seal of Approval is awarded. The ADA headquarters is located on the north side of Chicago. 1936: The ADA Council on Dental Education is formed. 1948: The National Institute of Dental Research (NIDR) is established (later renamed the National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research, NIDCR). 1950: The ADA collaborates with Congress to proclaim February 6 as National Children’s Dental Health Day and endorses water fluoridation. 1964: The ADA produces the first color television Public Service Announcement by a non-profit health agency and establishes the ADA Health Foundation, a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization for dental health research and education. 1970: ADA News is first published. 1978: The Council on Dental Practice is established. 1979: The Commission on Dental Accreditation is established. 1987: The ADA Commission on the Young Professional is formed (later becoming the Committee on the New Dentist). 1991: Dr. Geraldine Morrow becomes the first woman ADA president. 2002: Dr. Eugene Sekiguchi becomes the first minority ADA president. 2003: The first Give Kids a Smile day is held as part of National Children’s Dental Health Month.
